claim: Speed bugs and cards do not add memory; they turn a recall-and-subtract task into a perceptual proximity judgement (needle on the bug body = within 5 kt of Vref). Tools reshape the task.
agent_test: Compare an agent that must compute a check by reasoning vs one given an artefact that turns it into a lookup or pattern match (e.g. a tool that returns a diff or a pass/fail), same tokens.

claim: Cockpit memory is held in a chain of media (card, bug, spoken callout, pilot memory), computed at low-workload times and reused at high-workload times.
agent_test: Agent computes constants and thresholds early into a written ledger, then reads them back later; compare to recomputing in place.

claim: Redundant checking (two crew members, two indicators, challenge-response, callouts on deviation over 5 kt) is built into the practice, not added on.
agent_test: Add a second independent check step with a different view of the input; measure caught-error rate at equal tokens.

claim: Norman's thesis (artefacts change the task, not the person) is supported for external rules: externalised rules gave zero errors, all errors were on internal rules; the more rules externalised, the easier the problem.
agent_test: Move task rules from the prompt prose into an enforced structure (a table, a validator) and compare error rate.

claim: The representation matters, not only whether it is external: the same dimension carried by location was easier than by size or colour.
agent_test: Present the same state as a list, table or grid to the agent and compare accuracy.

claim: The cockpit claim that memory is a system property rests on description; Hutchins 1995 has no with-and-without test of bugs and no statistics.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; use as a caution on how strongly to cite it.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Checklist misuse and interruption are a real cause of accidents: three accidents in 15 months had checklist misuse as a probable cause; interruption broke the checklist.
agent_test: Interrupt the agent mid-procedure (inject a distractor turn) and measure skipped steps with and without an explicit step ledger.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Checklists cut harm in the original, enthusiastic, uncontrolled studies: WHO checklist deaths 1.5% to 0.8%, complications 11.0% to 7.0%; Keystone ICU infection median 2.7 to 0 per 1,000 catheter-days.
agent_test: Baseline for effect size claims; expect shrinkage in our tests.
audit_note: Minor: the Keystone intervention was a multi-part bundle (checklist plus other measures), and both were uncontrolled before-after designs, as the claim itself implies.

claim: Checklist effects shrink with stronger design and larger scale: Ontario mandate null (OR 0.91 and 0.97); Michigan surgery programme null (two studies); Matching Michigan ICUs: 1 of 17 units transformed. Local practice and enforcement decide.
agent_test: A guardrail text in the prompt is not enough; test whether enforcement (a gate that blocks) beats advice at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: all figures match (Ontario OR 0.91/0.97; Michigan Keystone Surgery null in registry and Medicare studies; Matching Michigan 1 of 17 units transformed); 'effects shrink with stronger design and larger scale' and 'enforcement decides' are the author's interpretation, and Matching Michigan was an English programme.

claim: Randomised and pooled evidence still favours WHO checklist for complications: stepped-wedge 19.9% to 11.5%; pooled RR 0.59 for any complication and 0.77 for mortality.
agent_test: Use as the upper bound; note 2024 review found only 13 of 93 studies of enough quality.

claim: Without outside feedback, LLM self-review does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 for GPT-4); gains in earlier work came from oracle labels.
agent_test: Run each check with and without a ground-truth signal (test, tool output) at equal tokens; keep only checks with an outside signal.
gap_search_note: Kamoi 2024 survey and CRITIC no-tool ablation agree (d06, d07).
audit_note: Minor: Huang et al. also shows small non-negative changes on HotpotQA, and the claim's 'often hurts' fits CommonSenseQA and GPT-4 GSM8K best; Kamoi et al. confirm that no prior work shows success from prompted self-feedback except in specially suited tasks.

claim: A sound external verifier gives the gain, and plain repeated sampling with the same verifier is a strong baseline (Game of 24: critique+verifier 36-38% vs sampling k=25 42%).
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: critique loop vs best-of-N with the same checker.
gap_search_note: CRITIC shows gain vanishes without the tool (HotpotQA F1 50.5 with, 46.1 without, equal to CoT).
audit_note: Minor: the sampling-vs-critique numbers (Game of 24: critique+sound verifier 36-38%, sampling k=25 42%) come only from Stechly et al.; on Blocksworld critique (83-87%) beat sampling (72%), so 'strong baseline' is domain-dependent; CRITIC supports only the general point that external tools drive the gain.

claim: Factored checks answered apart from the draft work better than joint ones (CoVe FACTSCORE 60.8 joint, 63.7 factored, 71.4 factor+revise; list precision 0.17 to 0.36).
agent_test: Run verification in a fresh context without the draft; compare to in-context verification.
gap_search_note: CoVe re-opened: factored beats joint by 1.5 to 4 points, but no equal-token or best-of-N control; stays single-source.

claim: Model-written YES/NO checklists improve judging (46.4% to 52.2% human agreement) and refinement (+7.8 LiveBench reasoning), and checklist rewards help training (+5.4 to 6.9% relative; CM2 +8 to +12).
agent_test: Generate a per-task checklist once, then grade final answer against it; compare to unstructured self-critique at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: the +7.8 LiveBench reasoning gain is for Command-R+ only (GPT-4o gained under 1 point overall); the CM2 gains (+8/+10/+12) are over an SFT baseline on tau-bench, BFCL-V4, ToolSandbox; RLCF gains are relative to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

claim: More checklist is not always better: skills that make validation mandatory caused 307 failures (67 from excessive verification), and a shown accurate checklist was less useful than a hard gate or self-written ledger.
agent_test: Vary number of check items (3, 8, 20) and measure accuracy and tokens; watch for over-verification cost.
gap_search_note: Degani & Wiener 1991 also argue long lists risk non-use; argued, not measured.

claim: Offloading intermediate state to an external trace or interpreter helps: scratchpad 8.8% to 20.1% few-shot; PAL 72.0 vs CoT 65.6; but asking the model to simulate the run in text gave only +4.5.
agent_test: Compare in-text arithmetic vs tool-executed arithmetic at equal tokens.
audit_note: Minor: scratchpad 8.8% to 20.1% is polynomial evaluation (few-shot), and the +4.5 is a PAL ablation where Codex 'executes' code in text (23.2 vs direct 18.7), so the three numbers are from different tasks; the scratchpad is itself written by the model, so 'external trace' is loose.

claim: Tool design changes what the same model can do: SWE-agent ACI beat shell-only by 10.7 points on Lite; no-lint editor 15.0 vs lint 18.0 vs no edit tool 10.3.
agent_test: Change only the tool interface (output format, linting) and hold the model fixed.

claim: Verification failure is a main failure class in multi-agent LLM systems (incorrect verification 9.10%, none 8.20%, premature stop 6.20% of traces).
agent_test: Count verification failure types in our own traces.

claim: Direct LLM tests of Hutchins' specific claim (a cockpit-style chain of media beats a single agent holding everything in context) are few; Cognitive Workspace reports 58.6% reuse vs 0% for RAG but is a self-reported preprint.
agent_test: Needs a controlled test; see GAPS.
gap_search_note: Still no direct controlled test of a two-checker design; nearest evidence: MoA +2.7 over SC (within noise), debate no better than voting, errors correlated across models.

claim: A hard gate that refuses state-violating actions beats the same state shown as advice, by a large margin, when the violation is decidable by code and the agent violates often. Gate: 0.98 vs shown checklist 0.55 to 0.59 (Qwen3-235B, 128 episodes per cell). It does nothing when the agent rarely violates, and hurts when the gate's own judgement is poor.
agent_test: For each guardrail G1-G12 pick one that code can decide (tests ran, number matches ledger). Run advice-only vs gate at equal tokens on our benchmarks and count violations and final accuracy.

claim: In an LLM-agent study with a self-written ledger, 24 of 26 and 20 of 20 on-turn re-executions fired with the step already marked DONE in the agent's own ledger, so re-reading its own record did not prevent redoing steps (though the ledger still beat an accurate checklist); and SOPBench requires the check calls to precede each service call, so a trajectory that skips them fails even if the final database state is correct.
agent_test: Log whether each guardrail check was actually executed (tool call or read-back), not only whether the agent says it was; report the gap.
audit_note: The counts (24 of 26 and 20 of 20 on-turn re-executions with the step already marked DONE) and SOPBench's procedure-completeness rule are accurate, but they show agents ignoring their own marks and a benchmark rule requiring verification calls, not marks written without action; the ledger arm actually beat the accurate checklist (0.70/0.79 vs 0.55/0.59), so 'compliance without doing' is not shown.
claim_before_audit: Written marks are not proof of action: agents with a self-written ledger still re-executed steps already marked done (24 of 26 and 20 of 20 on-turn re-executions), and SOPBench scores skipped check calls as failures even when the final state is right. Compliance without doing exists in LLM agents.

claim: Checks with an outside signal (interpreter, retrieval, tests) carry most of the gain in CRITIC: on text-davinci-003, CRITIC without the search tool equals plain CoT on QA F1 (HotpotQA 46.1 vs 46.1, AmbigNQ 58.3 vs 58.6, TriviaQA 74.7 vs 74.5) and loses 1.8 points on GSM8K program-of-thought (68.3 vs 70.1), though on ChatGPT and on TabMWP the tool-free variant still gains; Kamoi et al. find no prior work showing successful self-correction with feedback from prompted LLMs, except in tasks exceptionally suited to it.
agent_test: Label each check as tool-backed or self-review. Run each self-review check on and off on our benchmarks; drop those that do not help.
audit_note: Numbers match for text-davinci-003, but the generalisation fails: for ChatGPT, CRITIC w/o Tool beats CoT by about 3 F1 on HotpotQA (46.1 vs 42.8) and AmbigNQ (67.3 vs 64.3), and on TabMWP (davinci) w/o Tool still adds +20.3 over PoT, so 'flat or negative' is not general; Kamoi's finding is about feedback from prompted LLMs and has an exception clause.
claim_before_audit: Checks with an outside signal (interpreter, retrieval, tests) carry the gain; the same review without it is flat or negative. CRITIC without tools equals plain CoT on QA and loses 1.8 points on GSM8K program-of-thought; Kamoi's survey finds no reliable success for prompted self-feedback.

claim: At matched call or token budget, most of the apparent gain from a second reader or a debate is plain sampling and voting: self-consistency matches or beats debate and Reflexion (GSM8K 9 responses 88.2 vs 83.0 in Huang), voting accounts for most of MAD gains across 7 benchmarks, and the one counter-result is small (debate +1.3, MoA +2.7, interval about plus or minus 3 on n=1000).
agent_test: Any added checker arm must be compared to best-of-N with the same total tokens, not only to the single pass.

claim: LLM errors are correlated: across 350+ models, two wrong models agree 60% of the time on one dataset, more so for same-provider or larger models. A checker from the same model family gives much less redundancy than a second pilot. Independence has to come from a different view, a tool, or retrieval.
agent_test: Measure the overlap of missed errors between two same-model checkers, a different-view checker and a tool; use the pair with least overlap.

claim: Long-run decay comes from execution and from self-conditioning on one's own earlier errors, not only from missing knowledge: Qwen3-32B falls under 50% within 15 turns despite near-perfect single steps; thinking reduces the effect. This supports externalising state but is not a test of a verified ledger against recomputation.
agent_test: Long multi-step task with constants computed early: arm A recompute, arm B read from a ledger, arm C ledger plus read-back check; vary length 5, 10, 20, 40 steps.

claim: Interface-only changes move accuracy for a fixed model outside code: forced JSON/XML/YAML output lowers reasoning accuracy, and prompt template alone shifts GPT-3.5 by up to 40% on one task (GPT-4 less). Evidence is abstract-level only.
agent_test: For our checklist and tool outputs, test free text vs structured format on two models at equal tokens.

claim: The primary NASA report on cockpit checklists (Degani & Wiener 1991) contains no empirical skip rates; ASRS narratives are used as illustration and were not analysed statistically. Hull-loss concentration (76.3% of accidents in 27% of flight time) is the only count. Do not cite it for rates.
agent_test: None; citation hygiene.
